findings.summary: AMSD Ariadna, released in 1995 by Advanced Multimedia System Design, was the first Russian web browser. It targeted Windows 95 and Windows NT platforms and included features such as HTML 3.2 support, a 50,000-word English-Russian dictionary, and PNG image support with transparency. It lacked support for animated GIFs and JavaScript. Despite its technical merits, it was proprietary software and struggled to compete against dominant free browsers like Internet Explorer and Netscape Navigator in the Russian market, leading to its eventual discontinuation.

mechanisms.title: Platform compatibility and feature set
mechanisms.explanation: Ariadna was engineered specifically for early Windows environments (Windows 95 and Windows NT) and offered a curated feature set including HTML 3.2 rendering, dictionary lookup, and PNG transparency, while deliberately omitting animated GIF and JavaScript support.

mechanisms.title: Market positioning and discontinuation
mechanisms.explanation: As proprietary software released alongside dominant no-cost browsers, Ariadna failed to gain market traction in Russia and was terminated a few years after its introduction.
